tldr: For the fixed three-arm finite-population causal curvature contrast, the maintained spectral class admits an explicit uniform normal-approximation bound for the complete discontinuous scores whenever \(L_n=o(n^{1/3})\). A proved \(O(nL^3)\) tilted variance bound supports a total original-record interval with finite-sample coverage at least \(0.95\) on the entire maintained class and uniformly \(O_P(\sigma)\) halfwidth in that subregime. These upper results apply to a proper spectral subclass of the Guo--Liang--Toulis correlation elliptope. Legal non-Gaussian counterarrays for every \(\limsup_n L_n/\sqrt n>0\) also obstruct uniform normality on every larger class containing them. The sharp frontier remains open in the intermediate range \(n^{1/3}\lesssim L_n\ll\sqrt n\), together with the stronger cancellation-sensitive tilt bound and bounded-factor inference beyond the proved regime.
